description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—across different difficulty levels of a knowledge reasoning task, as referenced in the paper “Knowledge Crosswords: Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language Models.” The legend indicates that N+K+ is teal, N−K+ is tan, N−K− is orange, and N+K− is reddish-orange. In the “easy” chart, N−K+ dominates at 45.9%, followed by N+K+ at 40.6%, N−K− at 10.1%, and N+K− at 3.3%. The “medium” chart shows N+K+ at 44.6%, N−K+ at 44.3%, N−K− at 7.2%, and N+K− at 3.9%, indicating near parity between the two largest categories. In the “hard” chart, N−K− rises to 36.8%, N−K+ is 36.2%, N+K+ drops to 20.1%, and N+K− is 7.0%, suggesting a shift toward categories involving negative knowledge (K−) as difficulty increases. Each chart includes percentage labels inside the slices, and all slices are visually distinct with no exploded segments. The categories appear ordered roughly by size within each chart, though not strictly descending.
